rationale: A splits the work into small, well-named helper methods: _find, _build_parents, _reorient and _path_to. Its _reorient treats the tree as an undirected graph, combining children and parent as neighbours and skipping the node it came from, which is a clear and general way to re-root a tree. It also builds a completely new tree, so the result shares no nodes with the original. B finds the root-to-target path and rebuilds only the nodes on it with index-based loop logic. The comments explain it well, but it is more fiddly to follow. B reuses the original off-path subtrees inside the new tree, so a later change to either tree would show up in the other. B also defines nested helpers that are both named _find, inside two different methods. A is cleaner and more robust.
